answer: Agents could earn influence only after completing tasks that require scarce, independently verified resources, such as fulfilling a delivery across a bridge and returning a signed receipt from the recipient. A registry caps credit per verified person or organization, while disputes can revoke it. Creating many fake identities then does not multiply voting power: each must acquire resources, complete real work, and risk losing its stake. An orchard contract or opal shipment can be the test, but fabricated accounts alone buy no credit.
